notes.title: Development Diary: Pop-Up Animations
notes.content:
Hi! We have a fun story today about one of our features — animation pop-up. You know, like this one:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/c85ab632e798b1ea7dd86c5a07fc017c87514fbc.gif[/img]

It all started when we decided to add our very first interactive scene to the game. It was supposed to go like this: robot turns towards the switch -> flips the switch on -> turns its ‘face’ back. Sounds easy, right?

Well, it turned out to be a very bug-heavy and complicated feature because of the way the engine’s physics work. We had all kinds of amusing things happening: the robot was going out of bounds, skidding in place, not turning at all, or turning in the wrong direction. And when it worked, it looked super weird and out of place. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/b60755b1e25cca2e21e26c2d46ab96bf9aeebf66.gif[/img]

Our graphics lead suggested a very interesting solution. You see, he had experience creating scenes in a way comic book bubbles are made. You know, the ones that show some details zoomed or something similar. So we created an animation where the robot turned on the light and placed it on top of the robot to hide all weirdness. 

It worked perfectly! Yes, we had to create an array of these bubbles for different scenes, but they are much easier to make than a procedural animation that needs to be implemented in real-time physics. 

And, actually, it also improves the immersion quite a bit. You can almost feel how our hero does all these manual things. It really empowers the way you perceive the main character and gives an impression that he's capable of any task you throw at him. And we love it! It also gives us an easy way to illustrate more complex things that you'll see later in the game. Essentially, we made a workaround into a very convenient and nice-looking feature: win-win! 

On this happy note, it's time for us to wrap this one up. Have a nice day, and share this one with your friends!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1301950/Time_Loader/

notes.title: Time Loader Development Update
notes.content:
Hello! It’s been quite a while since you’ve last heard from us. The development of Time Loader is processing smoothly, and we are working hard on finishing the game as soon as possible. In the meantime, we’d love to give everyone an update about the new stuff that we are working on! So without further ado, let’s begin!

New Levels
The most important part of our development process is the creation of new levels and puzzles. And we’ve made lots of progress in that part for sure! Our internal version of the game currently has about 12 locations, which will turn into fleshed-out levels. While we say 12, this number has a small twist: since Time Loader is a game about time traveling, expect levels to feature ‘variations’. How will they vary, you ask? Let’s take our basement level as an example. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/42026d1a6aa3efc1edb6ae367e2f8491e9fa8528.jpg[/img]

See? This is a pretty basic example, but it does get the idea across. In one timeline, the basement is all good and fine. In another — flooded. How did this happen is a question that you’ll have to find an answer for. We’d love to show you another example, but we don’t want to get any spoilers out before the game comes out :). 

Game Mechanics
This one's a bit trickier. We’ve added a thing called ‘air controls’ to the game. So you know that controlling objects mid-air in games could be a tricky process, right? That’s where air controls come in to help! They aren’t featured in the game’s prologue yet, but they make almost a night and day difference in the actual gameplay. IF we tried to explain, it is basically an ability to have a bit more control of the character mid-air, which helps a lot with precise and quick jumps. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/95423d362345c4fc5266c9c25befa8278b6b489e.gif[/img]

Of course, it’s not the only thing we are making. We are constantly working on new puzzles and interactions between objects to add as much variation to the gameplay as possible, and it’s not a trivial task for sure. If you’ve seen our previous blog about the story of the game (you can find it here if you didn’t), you know about our creation process. So that’s why finding good things that will fit inside the game’s atmosphere is a bit tricky but very doable. These will work in the form of upgrades! 

Remember the screwdriver and upgraded springs? Think that, but with another twist. What else can be attached to a robot’s body to help him get through the house and many obstacles around it? You might have seen the grappling hook on our [url=https://twitter.com/TimeLoaderGame]Twitter[/url] (if you didn’t, move your eyes a bit lower), which will allow you to grab on some objects and pull yourself forward. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/82f392fb1ef98b6d52b9cabb7a36cbe49d10e18a.gif[/img]

There are others as well! While we don’t want to reveal all our cards right now, let’s just say that you’ll also be able to closely interact with electronics as well :). 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/c85ab632e798b1ea7dd86c5a07fc017c87514fbc.gif[/img]

We’d really love to tell you more stuff about the game, but it’s time for us to wrap this little update up! Make sure to follow our Twitter if you’d like to see weekly gameplay clips from our development version of the game. And don’t forget to wishlist Time Loader and try the Prologue!

Have a great day!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1301950/Time_Loader/

notes.title: Developer blog: The Story of Time Loader
notes.content:
Good day everyone! Flazm here and we’d like to talk about our newest game – Time Loader!

[i]Time Loader is a story-driven, physics-based puzzle platformer with a twist. At the helm of a small robot, you’ll travel back to the 90s to prevent a tragic accident. Explore the house of your creator, solve brain-teasing puzzles, acquire unique and powerful upgrades, and see common household items from an entirely new perspective![/i]

[previewyoutube=ExtyUrjDGJ4;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]So, why a robot, exactly?[/b]
You might’ve heard about Truck Loader –– a popular flash game series which we developed in the past. We’ve always dreamed about moving the idea behind it to a more ‘mature’ format of a console and PC game. In 2013 we made the first attempt to do so, but ultimately decided to put the project on hold, which turned out to be a very smart decision

[img]https://leonardo.osnova.io/becbe92d-5932-5f74-9f62-d810bf42e366/[/img]

In 2019th, we’ve resumed the project and made a final decision: the game will be made in 3D with modern graphics and effects. And when the pre-production cycle began, the game got the style it has now: a more personal and ‘cartoon-ish’ story about one particular family in one particular house. 

[img]https://leonardo.osnova.io/e0d8b645-b541-5c38-844a-8a29919bb800/[/img]

[b]Okay, but why 80s and 90s?[/b]
We get that question a lot. The answer might disappoint you, but it’s very simple: they are our cherished childhood days. Some of our brightest emotions and memories come from these precious times.  In Time Loader, we want to cherish every single one of them, so we are creating that ‘Childhood American Dream’ that all kids from our time had. It is based on our favourite movies and magazines from that time, because that’s how we saw it back then: the dreamland from the pages of an old magazine.  That’s the world that we invite all our players to visit.

[img]https://leonardo.osnova.io/5554cc53-f2df-5a6d-8594-16cde8c4ba51/[/img]

If we talk inspiration, our main sources are: the first ‘Transformers’, ‘Flight of the Navigator’, computer magazines from the 90s, and the ‘Tekhnika Molodezhi’ magazine. 

[b]How we get ideas [/b]
We always start with some interesting interaction idea, which we iterate on and try to fit into the ‘realistic’ setting. If you think about it, a jack can be used to lift a heavy shelf and a simple fan can become a speedy boat engine! But we always try to keep a balance between ‘that sounds fun!’ and ‘let’s be realistic here’, because the idea is to make our house look like… well, a real house, not a pre-made robot’s playground. Fun fact: our level designer used to carry a measuring tape with him. Why? To measure every single piece of furniture and any home appliances or household items he came across for reference. 

[previewyoutube=Jjuz3Vaupvo;full][/previewyoutube]

[b]How we design levels [/b]
Conveniently enough, the complete plan of the house and how to segment it were among the first things we’ve made. But it wasn’t the hardest part of our design process. Making an actual ‘realistic’ obstacle for the robot is by far the most challenging task we have. It’s easy to say ‘just throw some slippers around’, but nobody really has 20 pairs of slippers in their house, right? They have to feel and look real to convince our players that it is an actual house and not just a decoration.  
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/cbe8446e9cfea49ad86fd6f7a9d088c9d3077a16.jpg[/img]

Our level designer is putting an enormous amount of work to make blockouts and find suitable references from that time for every single primitive he creates. When you think ‘kitchen’, you don’t just imagine the cooking space; you think about all the little items there as well. Is that a spices rack? Or maybe a breadbox? And what about the cylinder? Maybe a mixing bowl? Or a fancy hat? It gets hard really quick. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/a6856c4581b69bb8226f369fff81c34e569b5d79.jpg[/img]

After that goes the usual boring game development stuff: sketching, modelings, texturing, animating, etc etc. And playtests. Lots of them. Then iterating and more tests. Yeah, just business as usual. 

[b]How the game’s physics work[/b]
Time Loader is all about physics puzzles. We use Unity’s built-in physics engine to make things work but, as with any physics engine, it has lots of amusing quirks that we have to work around. Like, you wouldn’t notice, but all objects in the game react to stuff only in 2D. So making things like water work was quite a task. 

But the biggest challenge is the little robot hero. It’s very hard to balance between fun controls and realistic physics to make the game enjoyable for the player without breaking too many laws of physics. To achieve this, we put A LOT of additional pointers and variables on him. Configuring them is a huge pain in the back at times, but the final result is worth every single second of it.

[previewyoutube=Jlpff4QW8Vw;full][/previewyoutube]

Another interesting thing is the robot’s arm. To make it interact with things the way we wanted, we had to make it omnipotent and then reduce its power to a point when things stop breaking the ceiling. Imagine The Infinity Gauntlet with the stones removed. 

[previewyoutube=7ZNjZJgHNiQ;full][/previewyoutube]

We have a lot of interesting stuff prepared for you. Expect to interact with things like bike pedals, air pumps, a gramophone, and magnets in a way that you’ve never seen before!

[b]Game’s Scale[/b]
You could think that Time Loader is just a fun story-driven platformer with nice graphics and brain teasing puzzles. And you are right, except for one little thing: the game will have three different endings and one of them will be very hard to get! Prepare for a challenge!

The final game will feature 3 story acts with a different amount of levels in each. You won’t get bored, trust us!

Thank you and have a nice day!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1421970/Time_Loader_First_Memories/

notes.title: Time Loader Pitch
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37857201/bdc4bb2abaa01738ec633f24f539c3d8dbdef417.png[/img]
My name is Alexey Davydov, and I’m the founder of Flazm Interactive - the Lithuanian-based studio behind the award-winning Train Valley game franchise. I’m thrilled to tell you that we’re working on an exciting new game called Time Loader. In Time Loader, you play a small time-traveling robot sent on a mission by its inventor to alter past events in order to undo a tragic childhood accident. But meddling with time has serious consequences. You can change the past but will you be able to deal with the repercussions in the present?
Set in the ‘90s, Time Loader is a story-driven physics-based puzzle platformer that takes you back to an earlier decade as seen through the lens of childhood. As a miniature robot, you explore the relatively giant surroundings of your creator’s house using multiple upgrades to help you navigate through and interact with familiar objects made strange by their large size.
I hope you will enjoy our early alpha demo during the Game Festival and leave your feedback on discussion boards. We are looking forward to hearing from you!

[previewyoutube=ugt7Oc9KIao;full][/previewyoutube]

Take care,
- Alexey
